subject: Comparatives and Superlatives

sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the comparative or superlative form of the adjectives in brackets:

questions.prompt: Tom is [gap] his brother. (old)

sections.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the comparative or superlative form. (Example: My hotel room was smaller than (small) the one in the photograph in the brochure.)
sections.contextText: I went on holiday last year but it was a disaster! My hotel room was smaller than the one in the photograph in the brochure.

questions.prompt: I think it was [gap] (small) room in the hotel.
The weather was terrible too. It was [gap] (cold) in England.
The beach near the hotel was very dirty – it was [gap] (dirty) all the beaches on the island.
The food was [gap] (expensive) I expected and I didn’t have enough money.
One day I went shopping in a big department store and I broke a vase. It was [gap] (expensive) vase in the whole shop.
But [gap] (bad) thing of all was that I lost my passport and I couldn’t go back home.
It was [gap] (horrible) holiday of my life.

sections.instruction: Read the passage and look at the chart. Compare Miss Bennet with her brother and her best friend Tina Robbins. (Example: Miss Bennet / tall / Tina Robbins → Miss Bennet is taller than Tina Robbins.)
sections.contextText:
Mr. and Mrs. Smith are now flying to Canada. Miss Bennet is their stewardess. She is very talkative and friendly. She is showing Mr. and Mrs. Smith some pictures of her family and her best friend.

Miss Bennet: This is my best friend. Her name is Tina.
Mrs. Smith: She is very pretty. Is she older or younger than you?
Miss Bennet: She is one year younger.
Mrs. Smith: Aren’t you thinner than she is?
Miss Bennet: Yes, I am. Tina loves to eat very much.
Mrs. Smith: So do I. I hope it will be time for lunch soon.

questions.prompt: Miss Bennet / short / her brother James
acceptedAnswers: Miss Bennet is shorter than her brother James.
Miss Bennet is shorter than her brother.
Miss Bennet is shorter than James.

questions.prompt: James / tall / her sister
acceptedAnswers: James is taller than his sister.
James is taller than her sister.
James is taller than Miss Bennet.

questions.prompt: Miss Bennet / old / her best friend
acceptedAnswers: Miss Bennet is older than her best friend.

questions.prompt: Her best friend / young / Miss Bennet
acceptedAnswers: Her best friend is younger than Miss Bennet.

questions.prompt: Miss Bennet / short / her brother
acceptedAnswers: Miss Bennet is shorter than her brother.

questions.prompt: Her brother / tall / Miss Bennet
acceptedAnswers: Her brother is taller than Miss Bennet.

questions.prompt: Miss Bennet / fat / Tina
acceptedAnswers: Miss Bennet isn't as fat as Tina.
Miss Bennet isn't fatter than Tina.
Miss Bennet isn't so fat as Tina.
questions.explanation: 57 kg vs 61 kg: use a negative comparison

questions.prompt: Tina / slim / Miss Bennet
acceptedAnswers: Tina isn't as slim as Miss Bennet.
Tina isn't slimmer than Miss Bennet.
Tina isn't so slim as Miss Bennet.
